title: Cap. 7 Scholastici: Cajetan on Romans 8 — special donation to the elect
pass_a_gloss: 6. Cajetan, on Romans 8, explaining these words, He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also give us all things? writes thus: Paul had noticed that the previously alleged reason of so many gifts did not efficaciously infer that God works all things unto good for the elect, but that God works with them unto good, and therefore, that he might efficaciously conclude that ALL THINGS, he added that God liberally gave even the Son for the elect, that from this he might infer that all things with the Son have been given to the elect. These sayings of Cajetan cannot be accommodated to that universal donation of Christ by which he is understood given to the whole world equally: for this being posited, God would give all things to all human beings equally: which is manifestly false. A certain special donation must therefore necessarily be conceded, according to which Christ is understood given to the elect alone, and which alone draws after itself an infallible and most certain donation of all things necessary unto salvation.
pass_b_english: 6. Cajetan on Romans 8: He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how will he not also with him give us all things? Paul saw that the earlier chain of gifts did not yet prove effectually that God works all things for the elect's good — only that he works with them unto good. So, to conclude ALL THINGS effectually, he added that God freely gave even the Son for the elect, and from that inferred that with the Son all things are given to them. Cajetan's words cannot be bent to a universal gift of Christ given equally to the whole world: if that were so, God would give all things equally to every human being — which is plainly false. A special donation must be granted, under which Christ is given to the elect alone, and which alone carries after it an infallible, most certain gift of everything needed for salvation.
source_text: 6. Cajetanus, in Rom. viii. explicans haec verba, Qui proprio Filio suo non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus eum tradidit, quomodo non cum illo omnia nobis donabit? sic scribit, Animadverterat Paulus, quod praeallegata ratio tot donorum non efficaciter inferebat Deum omnia in bonum electis cooperari, sed Deum illis cooperari in bonum, & propterea ut efficaciter concluderet quod OMNIA, adjinxit, quod Deus liberaliter donavit etiam Filium pro electis, ut hinc inferret quod omnia cum Filio electis donata sunt. Non possunt haec dicta Cajetani ad illam universalem Christi donationem accommodari, qua toti mundo datus ex aequo intelligitur: nam hoc posito, Deus omnia omnibus hominibus ex aequo daret: quod manifeste falsum est. Specialis ergo quaedam donatio necessario concedenda est, juxta quam Christus solis electis datus intelligatur, & quae sola trahat post se infallibilem & certissimam donationem omnium rerum ad salutem necessariarum.
